sections.title: Pharmacist courses in France
sections.lead: In \\pharmacy courses in France\\, there is a professional degree track and related courses in \\pharmaceutical and health sciences\.

items: Common selections are:
Doctor of Pharmacy:
Pharmaceutical Sciences: Research involving medicines, \\drug formulation, pharmacology and pharmaceutical chemistry.
Master's in Pharmaceutical Sciences: Further education in drug development, pharmaceutical technology, and research.
Pharmaceutical Industry: Courses on production, quality assurance, regulatory affairs, and drug development.
Pharmacy Residency and Specialisation: Further training for qualifying students on particular specialist career paths.
Pharmacy Technician Training: Vocational training programs such as the \\DEUST with a professional scope different from the pharmacist qualification
The typical \\pharmacist pathway in France\\ takes \\a minimum of six years\. Some specialty tracks, like pharmacy residency, take longer to complete.

sections.title: Admission requirements to study pharmacy in France
sections.lead: Depending on your nationality, previous qualifications and the course you want to study-

items: Common considerations include:
Secondary education equivalent to the French baccalauréat for admission through the first-year route.
Good background knowledge of \\science subjects\\, especially \\chemistry and biology\.
Fulfill the university's \\admission and selection requirements\.
Sufficient \\French language proficiency\\ for academic and clinical study.
Official recognition / evaluation of previous qualifications (where applicable.

Entry to the professional pharmacy program is normally by a recognized first year health-studies route such as \\PASS or [L.AS](http://L.AS)\\ Progression to pharmacy is competitive and not guaranteed by simply passing the first year.

sections.title: Cost of studying pharmacy in France
sections.lead: The overall \\cost of studying pharmacy in France\\ will depend on the university, the applicant category, the \\tuition fee policy\\ and the city.

items: Fees
Public universities publish registration fees, but international students can be exempt or pay differentiated fees.
For reference, the published fee schedule for the first cycle at France's standard public universities for eligible student categories has been \\€178 per year\.
This is \\not a guaranteed total fee for all international pharmacy students. Additional costs and different fee rules may apply.
Students must budget for:
\\Housing and utilities\.
Food and day to day expenses.
\\Public transport. - Health insurance or other applicable health care costs.
Study costs (books, laboratory material etc.)
\\Visa and administration fees\\ , if applicable.
Cost of living varies from city to city and Paris can be more expensive than other university towns. Before you accept an offer, create a truthful monthly budget.

sections.title: Admission Procedure for Pharmacy in France
sections.lead: \\Pharmacies in France\\ Admission depends on your qualifications and where you live.

items: 1. \\Choose a program:\\ Decide whether you want the \\professional pharmacy degree\\, a related master's program or another pharmaceutical course.
2. \\Check eligibility:\\ Make sure your previous qualifications meet the requirements of the university.
3. \\Choose the application path:\\ The steps may differ for first year health studies, later year admission and master applications.
4. \\Gather documents:\\ Collect your transcripts, proof of identity, proof of language skills and any other supporting documents that may be requested.
5. \\Complete selection procedures:\\ Submit further documents or attend an interview if required.
6. \\Accept your offer:\\ Register and follow the instructions of the university.
7. \\Get your visa\\: If applicable, follow the \\official French student-visa procedure\.

Students applying from India should refer to \\Campus France India\\ and the respective university. Some of the routes available for candidates with foreign health qualifications have special procedures and deadlines.

sections.title: Accreditation and Recognition of Pharmacy in France
sections.lead: The state diploma of the \\professional pharmacy pathway\\ is the French \\\Diplôme d'État de docteur en pharmacie\\\ . Moreover, graduates need to meet the relevant \\professional registration and practice requirements\\ to be able to practice as a pharmacist in France.

items: The professional pharmacist diploma and a \\Master of Pharmaceutical Sciences\\ or a \\pharmacy-related technician qualification\\ are not the same.
\\Indian students:\\

If you want to practise as a pharmacist in India, find out the current \\qualification-recognition and registration requirements\\ from the \\Pharmacy Council of India\\ and the authorities concerned before enrolling.

faqs.q: How many years of studying Pharmacy in France?
faqs.a: The standard \\professional pharmacy pathway in France\\ lasts \\at least six years. Some specialist routes may take longer.

faqs.q: Do international students study pharmacy in France?
faqs.a: Yes, \\international students\\ may be eligible but entry requirements and application procedures are dependent on nationality, previous qualifications and the program chosen.

faqs.q: Do I need to speak French to study pharmacy in France?
faqs.a: The majority of \\professional pharmacy studies\\ are taught primarily in French. Students should check the language requirements of the faculty they choose and be ready for professional communication during placements.

faqs.q: Is it possible to become a pharmacist in India after studying in France?
faqs.a: You have to check the \\recognition and registration requirements\\ with the \\Pharmacy Council of India\\ and other appropriate authorities. "A French qualification does not mean that you can automatically practice in India.
